solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heroine of novel, literary — what will author do about the French name?

parts.note: LIT is the usual short form of literary, as in lit crit

indicators.note: the verb is wrapped about the other pieces, which sit inside it

parts.note: an author will tell a story
le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question about a novel's heroine, wondering what her author will do with a French name.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Nell Trent is the heroine of Dickens's novel The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: One reveres union agreement subsequently

parts.note: 'I do' is the vow of agreement spoken at a wedding, a union of two people
later means subsequently, afterwards

explanation.surface: Someone respects a trade union deal that is made afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union but is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, so is a person who reveres something to excess.

clue.text: Hard problem? Heading off to fiddle

indicators.note: the word's heading, its first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a stinker is slang for a very difficult problem

explanation.surface: Facing a tough problem, someone sets off to play the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' removes the S from the front of STINKER.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle about with something, making small idle adjustments.

clue.text: Quits ale, changing — to these?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker gives up beer and switches, perhaps to a stronger Mexican spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone who quits ale might change to these.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit, a plausible drink to switch to after giving up beer.

clue.text: Priests inviting millions in for harvest festival

indicators.note: the priests invite the letter in, so it goes inside them

parts.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist priests or monks
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Clergy welcoming huge numbers to a harvest celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Lammas (1 August) is the old English festival of the first wheat harvest, from 'loaf mass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas was the traditional English feast celebrating the first loaves baked from the new harvest.

clue.text: Regret picking up old coin

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone sorry they picked up a worthless antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old coin' looks like one phrase, but 'old' gives O and only 'coin' defines; the euro is current.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency coin used across most of the European Union.

clue.text: Difficulty about league team's weak point

indicators.note: the difficulty goes about, around, the abbreviation

parts.note: a bind is an awkward difficulty
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A football pundit spotting trouble with a league side's weak spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside BIND, giving BLIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind side is the direction someone cannot see, hence a vulnerable spot or weakness.

clue.text: Servant's a busy fellow, sending son packing

indicators.note: with packing, sending packing means dismissing, so a letter is removed
completes the phrase sending packing, to send away

parts.note: a bustler is someone always busy and bustling about

explanation.surface: A household servant is a busy chap who dismisses the son of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending ... packing' removes the S from BUSTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household.

clue.text: Erotic art lacking heart — endlessly boring instead

indicators.note: the middle letter of art is lost, leaving its ends
something takes the place of the lost heart
the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: dull means boring

explanation.surface: A critic finds the erotic art heartless and dull instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult used of films or books means sexually explicit, so erotic.

clue.text: Reasonable numbers seen around in rising sport

indicators.note: the numbers are seen around, outside, the other piece

parts.note: tens are round numbers, reasonable ones to work with

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Sensible attendance figures for a sport growing in popularity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: Waste a little drink (most of beer)

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone squanders a dram and most of a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims ALE to AL. To total a car, chiefly American slang, is to wreck it.
explanation.definitionFit: To total something is to wreck it completely, laying it waste.

clue.text: Old instrument, strange, with tips of metal hooks enclosed in metal band

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the band's name

parts.note: Korn is an American nu-metal band
rum means odd or strange

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A strange antique instrument held together with metal hooks inside a metal ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal band' looks like a metal ring, but is a rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: The krummhorn is a Renaissance capped double-reed instrument with a hooked end.

clue.text: Franchise ultimately precedes a roll etc possibly described thus?

definitions.text: Franchise ultimately precedes a roll etc possibly described thus?

indicators.note: the letter goes before the rest
the final letter of the word is taken
the letters are rearranged into one possible order

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a voters' list might be described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A ROLL ETC into LECTORAL. The whole clue defines: the franchise (the vote) leads to an electoral roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The register of voters is the electoral roll, and the franchise is the right to vote.

clue.text: Vessel mostly filled with American food

indicators.note: the shortened word is filled with the other piece
all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat largely loaded with American provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Fun etc. is, if organised, ample

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: If properly organised, fun and the like is plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufficient means enough, and ample means more than enough, so the two are close.

clue.text: Soil shortage (no depth)

indicators.note: no means the letter is absent from the word

parts.note: a dearth is a shortage

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a lack of soil, too shallow for planting.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the loose ground in which plants grow, the same as soil.

clue.text: Endless twist about drop in European capital

indicators.note: the shortened word goes about, around, the other
the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a helix is a spiral twist
to sink is to drop

explanation.surface: A spiral round a fall somewhere in a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Hands back farthing with disdainful response

indicators.note: the word is read back to front

parts.note: fins is slang for hands
F is the abbreviation for farthing, an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny

explanation.surface: Someone handing back a measly farthing with a contemptuous snort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FINS into SNIF. A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniff is a short audible intake of breath expressing scorn or contempt.

clue.text: I note attractions providing more thoughtful pieces of information

parts.note: sights are tourist attractions

explanation.surface: A tourist notes the attractions that offer deeper information.
explanation.definitionFit: Insights are perceptive understandings, deeper than mere facts or data.

clue.text: Hero of series to wander aimlessly

definitions.meaning: Harry, the boy wizard of J K Rowling's book series

explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter is the title hero of the novels, and to potter is to move about idly.

clue.text: Lead programme finally involving garden goddess

indicators.note: the outer pieces involve, enclose, the other

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to hoe is to work the garden

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A gardening programme's lead presenter finally features a goddess of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a Titan goddess of Greek myth, and a byname of Artemis as moon goddess.

clue.text: Couple done over after clipping wings of little baby bird

indicators.note: the reversed word clips, holds, the other letters inside
the word is turned over, back to front

parts.note: a couple is two

indicators.note: the outer letters, the wings, of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A pair beaten up after clipping the wings of a small fledgling.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, so a baby bird.

clue.text: Carefully adapt shadow military force

parts.note: to tail someone is to shadow them
OR, other ranks, means the soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An instruction to fit a covert surveillance operation to the army's needs.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to adjust it to fit a particular need or purpose.

clue.text: Shock broadcast of story without foundation doing for security expert

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mass of locks

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: a myth is an untrue story

explanation.surface: An alarming report of a groundless tale, featuring a security specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a fright; it is a mass of hair. The word for an untrue story, said aloud, ends the answer with the spelling MITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and repairs locks, so is an expert in security.

clue.text: Light punishment restricting originators of dodgy loans

indicators.note: the punishment restricts, encloses, the other letters

parts.note: the cane was a school punishment

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A lenient sentence for those who set up dodgy loans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective describing the punishment, but it is the noun defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle is a wax stick with a wick, burned to give light.

clue.text: Spies attending opening of play after tense note from strategist

indicators.note: the play's opening comes after the tense
the spies attend, sit beside, the opening act

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
Act I is the opening act of a play
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Secret agents at a play's opening night, nervously noting a master planner.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician plans moves cleverly, in the manner of a strategist.

clue.text: Film speed

definitions.meaning: a short extract from a film

explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a brief excerpt of film, and a good clip is a brisk pace.

clue.text: Forbidding European filth

parts.note: grim means stern and forbidding

explanation.surface: A stern European complaining about dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is ingrained dirt, so filth.

clue.text: Big animal runs hard into no end of forest

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: no means the letter is taken out
the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A large beast charges hard into the depths of the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' reads as a link word but is a piece: 'no end of forest' removes T from INTO, giving INO.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a huge, thick-skinned, horned animal.

clue.text: Large quantity, on being swallowed by cattle, produces much explosive power

indicators.note: the pieces are swallowed, taken inside, the cattle

parts.note: kine is an archaic plural of cow, meaning cattle
a lot is a large quantity

explanation.surface: A huge amount, once swallowed by cows, produces tremendous wind power.
explanation.walkthrough: KINE is an old plural meaning cows.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilotonne is a unit of explosive force equal to a thousand tonnes of TNT.
